review: The hymn is the shed blood as a call to the unconverted: 1:1–4 is 1 Pet 1:19 with Rom 5:8, 2:1–4 is Zech 13:1 with Isa 53:10 and Heb 10:29, 3:1–4 is Luke 13:25 with Prov 1:24–28, and 4:1–4 is John 14:6 with Acts 4:12 and Rom 10:9.

2:2 וְהַמִּשְׁפָּט כְּבָר שָׂבַע — the Arabic وَالْعَدْلُ قَدِ اكْتَفَى is 'justice is content'; the Hebrew uses שָׂבַע, the satisfaction verb of Isa 53:11 (יִשְׂבַּע), so the line is the finished satisfaction of the law and not merely a legal pause.

3:3–4 keep the print's warning in the second person singular and the reversal (weeping, unaccepted), with the Hebrew נֶעֱנָה negated, because the stanza's force is that the door closes while the knocking continues.
